enDesc: A commentary focusing on Rabbi Mordechai Yoffe's Levush Malkhut, which distinguishes and explains the reasons for his disagreements with the Shulchan Arukh, it became one of the main commentaries on the Shulchan Arukh itself.

title: שערי תשובה על שולחן ערוך אורח חיים
enTitle: Sha'arei Teshuvah on Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim
enDesc: Commentary on Orach Chaim section of Shulchan Arukh, which includes extracts from other Halakhic works and responsa not appearing in "Ba'er Hetev," along with the author's own insights. It was completed posthumously by his brother, R' Ephraim Zalman, and appears in most editions of the Shulchan Arukh.
enShortDesc: Collection of responsa and rulings that were not included in the Be'er Hetev. Written in the 19th century by Rabbi Chaim Mordekhai Margaliot.
heDesc: פירוש על שולחן ערוך אורח חיים, הכולל תמצית של דברי הפוסקים שלא הובאו ב"באר היטב," בנוסף לחידושים מהמחבר עצמו. החיבור הושלם לאחר מותו על ידי אחיו, ר' אפרים זלמן, והוא מופיע ברוב המהדורות של השולחן ערוך.
heShortDesc: פירוש המלקט תשובות ופסקים שלא הובאו בבאר היטב, נכתב במאה ה-19 על ידי הרב חיים מרדכי מרגליות.

title: ספר המצוות
enDesc: The Sefer HaMitzvot (“Book of Commandments”) is Maimonides’ list of the 613 commandments accompanied by brief descriptions, originally written in Arabic. It was meant to serve as an introduction to his magnum opus and legal code, the Mishneh Torah. The work’s introduction details 14 principles that guided the selection of commandments and delivers harsh criticism to previous attempts to enumerate the commandments, particularly that of the Halakhot Gedolot. Many later works, including the Sefer HaChinukh, rely on the enumeration of commandments in the Sefer HaMitzvot.
enShortDesc: Maimonides’ list of the 613 commandments with brief descriptions, originally written in Arabic.
heShortDesc: חיבור שנכתב על ידי הרמב"ם במאה ה-12, בו הוא מונה ומפרט את תרי״ג מצוות התורה. נכתב במקור בערבית.

title: לב שמח
enDesc: 17th-century work by Rabbi Avraham Aligri defending Maimonides’ Sefer HaMitzvot against the attacks of Nachmanides. The title of this work is a hint to the author's name "Aligri", which is Italian for "glad of heart".
enShortDesc: 17th-century work by Rabbi Avraham Aligri defending Maimonides’ Sefer HaMitzvot against the attacks of Nachmanides.
heDesc: ביאור לספר המצוות להרמב"ם. (שם הספר "לב שמח" הוא רמז לשם המחבר "אליגרי", שכך משמעותו באיטלקית.)

title: השגות הרמבן על ספר המצוות
enDesc: In this work, the Ramban (Nachmanides) defends Simeon Kayyara (8th Century) against criticisms put forth in Rambam’s (Maimonides) Sefer HaMitzvot.

title: מגילת אסתר על ספר המצוות
enDesc: Commentary on Rambam's Sefer HaMitzvot, in which the author defends Rambam from the criticisms of Ramban.
enShortDesc: Commentary on Rambam's Sefer HaMitzvot
heDesc: פירוש לספר המצות להרמב"ם, בו המחבר מגין על הרמב"ם מהשגותיו של הרמב"ן.

title: ספר המצות הקצר
enDesc: The Sefer HaMitzvot HaKatzar (Concise Book of Commandments) is an abbreviated reworking of Maimonides’ Sefer HaMitzvot that only includes commandments applicable outside of Israel in the post-Temple era, written by Rabbi Yisrael Meir HaKohen Kagan, author of the Mishnah Berurah and the Chafetz Chaim. In the work’s introduction, Kagan explained that he wanted his audience to be able to easily access a list of commandments applicable to their lives, and sifting through the Sefer HaMitzvot to isolate the relevant ones would be cumbersome.
enShortDesc: 20th-century list of the commandments applicable outside of Israel in the post-Temple era.
heDesc: חיבור קטן מאת ר' ישראל מאיר הכהן מראדין, בעל ה'חפץ חיים', בו נאספו ונלקטו כל המצוות עשה ולא תעשה שאפשר לקיימן בזמן הזה, עם ביאור קצר ותמציתית.
heShortDesc: רשימה מן המאה ה-20 של כל המצוות החלות בחוץ לארץ ישראל לאחר חורבן בית המקדש.

title: ספר מצוות קטן
enDesc: Sefer Mitzvot Katan (“The Small Book of Commandments,” also referred to by its Hebrew acronym, the Semak) is a 13th-century poetic abridgment of the [Sefer Mitzvot Gadol](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefer_Mitzvot_Gadol?tab=contents) of [Moses of Coucy](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/moses-ben-jacob-of-coucy). It blends laws, stories, and ethical teachings, omitting commandments not applicable in the post-Temple era as well as the extensive legal discussions of the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol. The book was originally titled "Sheva Amudei HaGolah" (“The Seven Pillars of the Exile”) because it is divided into seven parts corresponding to the days of the week, in order to encourage daily review. It achieved widespread popularity and was included by some early authorities in the prayer book so that the precepts could be recited daily.
enShortDesc: 13th-century poetic abridgment of the Sefer Mitzvot Gadol that blends laws and stories, also known as the Semak
heDesc: חיבור הלכתי המהווה סוג של קיצור ל"ספר מצוות גדול" (סמ"ג), כשהוא משמיט את הדיונים הארוכים ומספק תמצית של כל מצוה. הוא גם השמיט כל המצוות שאינן נהוגות בזמן הזה. הספר נקרא במקורו "שבע עמודי הגולה" בשל העובדה שהוא מחולק לשבעה חלקים המקבילים לימי השבוע, כדי לעודד ולהקל על לימוד וחזרה תמידית. אכן, הספר זכה לפופולריות ולתפוצה רבה בקהילות ישראל השונות, וקיבל הכרה מיוחדת מחכמי צרפת וגרמניה, עד כדי כך שהיו מקומות שכללו אותו בתוך סידורי התפילה כדי שיעיינו בו בכל יום במקום אמירת מזמורי תהלים ותחינות.
heShortDesc: קיצור של 'ספר מצוות גדול', המשלב הלכות וסיפורי מעשה. ידוע בכינוי המקוצר 'סמ"ק'.

title: קיצור ספר חרדים
enTitle: Kitzur Sefer Haredim of Rabbi Elazar Azcari
enDesc: Kitzur Sefer Haredim is a 19th-century abridgment of Rabbi Elazar Azcari’s Sefer Haredim, a 16th-century ethical-kabbalistic treatise. Kitzur Sefer Haredim focuses on listing the commandments and unconventionally ordering them according to the body parts used in their performance. It was also called Mitzvat Moshe in its first publication, printed in the back of the author’s “Zichru Torat Moshe” on the laws of Shabbat.
enShortDesc: 19th-century work listing the commandments according to the body parts that perform them.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-19 המונה ומחלק את תרי״ג מצוות התורה על פי איברי הגוף הנדרשים לקיום כל מצווה.

title: ספר יראים
enDesc: Sefer Yereim (“The Book of those who Fear”) is a 12th-century legal work that incorporates ethical teachings, based on the enumeration of the 613 commandments in the Halakhot Gedolot. The work consists of 417 commandments, not 613, since some commandments are grouped together. In his introduction to the work, Rabbi Eliezer explains that he chose its title to reflect his intention that “from [this book], people will learn to fear God.” Later legal authorities often quote the Yereim and consider it authoritative.
enShortDesc: 12th-century legal work that incorporates ethical teachings, based on the Halakhot Gedolot.
heDesc: ספר מיוסד על תרי"ג המצוות לפי שיטת רב יהודאי גאון (בה"ג), הכולל עניני הלכה ודברי מוסר. הספר יצא לאור בשלימותו עם ביאור רחב בווילנא בשנת 1889.
heShortDesc: חיבור הלכתי מן המאה ה-12 המבוסס על ספר 'הלכות גדולות', ומשולבים בו גם דברי מוסר.

title: ספר המצוות לרסג
enDesc: The Sefer HaMitzvot of Rasag (“Book of Commandments of Rav Saadia Gaon”) is a 10th-century piyyut (liturgical poem) that concisely summarizes the 613 commandments, with each commandment described in only a few words. The work is well-known for an extensive analytic commentary that Rabbi Yerucham Fishel Perlow wrote on it in the 20th century.
enShortDesc: 10th-century poem that concisely summarizes the 613 commandments.
heShortDesc: פיוט מן המאה ה-10 המונה ומסכם בקצרה את תרי״ג מצוות התורה.

title: מנחת חינוך
enDesc: The Minchat Chinukh (“Offering of Education”, a play-on-words referencing a Temple sacrifice of the same name) is a legal commentary on the Sefer HaChinukh. It does not present practical conclusions but rather conceptual analysis, posing questions, problems, and uncommon test cases. Many subsequent commentaries were written on the Minchat Chinukh, and it is considered an important starting point for theoretical analysis of the commandments.
enShortDesc: 19th-century work that conceptually analyzes the legal parts of the Sefer HaChinukh.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-19 המציע ניתוח רעיוני לחלקים ההלכתיים בספר החינוך.

title: ספר החינוך
enDesc: The Sefer HaChinukh (“Book of Education”) is an anonymous work written in thirteenth-century Spain that clearly details the 613 commandments and explains the reasons behind them. In his introduction, the author explains that he wrote the book to “awaken the hearts'' of his teenage son and his peers, hoping to foster in them a sense of connection to the commandments. For each commandment, the author cites a biblical source, addresses the philosophical underpinnings of the commandment, presents a brief overview of the details of its observance, and summarizes the commandment’s applicability. The work remains popular today, especially in educational settings.
enShortDesc: Anonymous medieval work detailing and explaining the 613 commandments.
heDesc: ספר החינוך מבאר את תרי"ג המצוות, מסודר לפי פרשיות התורה. המחבר של הספר כותב בהקדמתו שחיברו כדי "לעורר לב הנער בני והילדים חביריו בכל שבוע ושבוע, אחר שילמדו אותו הסדר בחשבון המצות, ולהרגיל אותם בהם ולהתפיס מחשבתם במחשבת טהרה וחשבון של עיקר, טרם שיכניסו בלבם חשבונות של שחוק ושל מה לך ומה בכך, וגם כי יזקינו לא יסורו ממנו"...  המחבר מזהה עצמו רק כ"איש יהודי מבית לוי ברצלוני", ויש חילוקי דעות לגבי זהותו המדויקת. יש המייחסים את הספר לר' אהרן הלוי (רא"ה), אבל כבר הוכח בבירור שהוא לא חיברו. אחרים מיחסים אותו לר' פנחס הלוי, אחיו של הרא"ה. היחודיות של ספר החינוך הוא בזה שמלבד דיני המצוה, המחבר דן גם בשרשיו וטעמו, שלא כספרים הלכתיים אחרים.
heShortDesc: חיבור אנונימי מימי הביניים המונה ומפרט את תרי״ג מצוות התורה.

title: ספר מצוות גדול
enDesc: Sefer Mitzvot Gadol (“Great Book of Commandments,” also referred to by its Hebrew acronym, the SeMaG) is a 13th-century work composed in France that enumerates the 613 commandments. Based on Maimonides’ Mishnah Torah, which is quoted on every page, the work marks the penetration of the Sephardic Maimonides into Ashkenazic legal works. The Semag also incorporates sources from Talmud, Midrashim, and early French and German commentators, and includes legal discussions and moral teachings. Its great influence as a legal source and guidebook is evidenced by the large number of manuscripts preserved and the many commentaries that the work inspired. In the era preceding the publication of the Shulchan Arukh, the Semag was the principal legal text studied in Ashkenazic academies.
enShortDesc: 13th-century text enumerating and elaborating upon the commandments, also known as the Semag.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-13 המונה ומפרט את תרי״ג מצוות התורה ואת העקרונות לספירה זו. מוכר בכינויו המקוצר 'סמ"ג'.

title: בן איש חי
enDesc: Ben Ish Chai (“Son of a Living Man”), is a collection of sermons on the Torah blended with mystical insights and Sephardic legal rulings, based on sermons that the author delivered to his congregation. It is studied extensively and is a standard reference work for many Sephardic Jews, much like its Ashkenazi counterpart, the Kitzur Shulhan Arukh. It is known for its strict rulings, many of which are based upon kabbalistic teachings.
enShortDesc: Sermons on the Torah blended with mystical insights and Sephardic legal rulings.
heDesc: ספר ה"בן איש חי" הוא היצירה המפורסמת ביותר של החכם יוסף חיים. הספר הוא אוסף הלכות לענייני היום-יום, בליווי תובנות ומנהגים מיסטיים. הוא מיועד להמונים, ומסודר לפי סדר הפרשות השבועיות. התפוצה הרחבה של הספר הפכה אותו לכתובת סטנדרטית לבירור שאלות הלכתיות בעולם ההלכה הספרדי, והוא מתפקד כקיצור ל"שולחן ערוך", בדומה למקבילתו האשכנזית, ה"קיצור שולחן ערוך".
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-19 שבו מסודרת ההלכה הספרדית על פי דרשות קצרות על פרשיות השבוע, תוך שילוב של גימטריות ורעיונות מחכמת הקבלה.

title: טור
enDesc: The Tur, also known as Arba’ah Turim (“The Four Rows"), an allusion to the jewels on the high priest’s breastplate), is a 14th-century legal code by Rabbi Jacob ben Asher. It traces Jewish law from the Bible through the Talmud and early legal authorities, citing the author’s opinions as well as dissenting opinions. The work is divided into four sections that cover all areas of practical law, excluding laws that are only relevant in Temple times. Many commentaries were written on the Tur, most prominent among them Rabbi Joseph Karo’s “Beit Yosef,” which formed the basis of the Shulchan Arukh. Study of the Tur alongside its commentaries and the Shulchan Arukh is of primary importance in traditional yeshivas.
enShortDesc: 14th-century comprehensive legal code by Jacob ben Asher, upon which the Shulchan Arukh is based.
heShortDesc: חיבור הלכתי מקיף מהמאה ה-14 שחובר על ידי יעקב בן אשר, עליו מבוסס השולחן ערוך.

title: בית יוסף
enDesc: Beit Yosef, by Rabbi Joseph Caro, is a long, detailed commentary on the Arba'ah Turim. ‎It ‎served as a precursor to the Shulhan Arukh, which Rabbi Caro wrote later in his life. Karo began ‎the ‎Beth Yosef in 1522 at Adrianople, finished it in 1542 at Safed in the Land of Israel; he published ‎it in ‎‎1550–59. This work analyzes the theories and conclusions of the Tur and opinions of authorities ‎not ‎mentioned by the latter. Karo evidences not only an astonishing range of reading, covering ‎almost ‎the entire rabbinic literature up to his time, but also remarkable powers of critical ‎investigation. He ‎evidences no inclination to simply accept the opinions of ancient authorities, ‎notwithstanding his ‎great respect for them.‎ Despite Caro's own preference for the Beit Yosef, it ‎was his shorter work Shulhan Arukh, which he wrote for students and ignorami that became ‎authoritative.‎

title: בח
enDesc: Written by Joel Sirkes (1561-1640) in Poland, Bayit Chadash (Bach) is a classic commentary on the Tur, printed in most editions alongside Beit Yosef. The Bach explains the text, provides sources and occasionally offers a dissenting opinion from that of Beit Yosef.
heDesc: "בית חדש" (ב"ח) הוא פירוש על הארבעה טורים, נדפס ברוב מהדורות של הטור ליד פירושו של ר' יוסף קארו "בית יוסף".

title: פרישה
enDesc: One of two classic commentaries on the Tur by Rabbi Joshua Falk, the Prisha is made up of explanation of the legal decisions of the Tur.

title: דרכי משה
enDesc: Rama's commentary on Tur, originally written in greatly expanded form, was subsequently shortened when the author became aware that Beit Yosef had completed a similar work. Rama then condensed his work and included only the material which complements Beit Yosef's work. The text of Darchei Moshe which is printed together with Tur is a further abridged version, with the complete version printed separately in the back of many editions of Tur.
heDesc: פירוש הרמ"א לטור, בתחילה נכתב מבלי לדעת שגם ר' יוסף קארו עובד על משהו דומה, וכשהשלים החלק על אורח חיים נודע לו שכבר יצא לאור הספר "בית יוסף", ולכן הוא קיצר את ספרו ועשהו מעין השלמה על ה"בית יוסף". ה"דרכי משה" שנדפס בדפי הטור הוא גם מקוצר ממה שהוציא המחבר, והפירוש השלם נדפס בסוף הכרך בפני עצמו ברוב מהדורות הטור.

title: דרישה
enDesc: One of two classic commentaries on the Tur by Rabbi Joshua Falk, Drisha (investigation) is composed of analyses spun off of questions on the legal decisions of the Tur.

title: קיצור שלחן ערוך
enDesc: The Kitzur Shulchan Arukh (“Abridged Shulchan Arukh”) is a simplified summary of the Shulchan Arukh, focusing on Orach Chayim and Yoreh De’ah, the sections most relevant to ordinary daily life. The work presents laws without listing differing views or providing reasoning, interspersing ethical maxims throughout. Immensely popular for its simplicity and clarity, it functions as a handbook for daily life for many Ashkenazi Jews and has been translated into five languages. It is known for its strict rulings.
enShortDesc: Popular handbook with simplified summaries of laws relevant to daily life, published in 1864.
heDesc: "קיצור שולחן ערוך" הוא סיכום של ה"שולחן ערוך" של ר' יוסף קארו, עם התייחסות לפירושים מאוחרים יותר. הקיצור כותב באופן ברור ובלתי משתמע לשני פנים מה מותר ומה אסור. גאנצפריד הדגיש את מנהגי יהודי הונגריה בזמנו. החיבור נכתב באופן מוצהר כטקסט פופולרי, ותפוצתו הרחבה הפכה אותו לכתובת סטנדרטית לבירור שאלות הלכתיות, כאשר הוא מתפקד כקיצור ל"שולחן ערוך", בדומה למקבילתו הספרדית, ה"בן איש חי." גאנצפריד ביסס את פסיקותיו על שלושה סמכויות הלכתיות אשכנזיות: ר' יעקב לורברבוים, מחבר "דרך החיים", ר' שניאור זלמן מלאדי, מחבר "שולחן ערוך הרב", ור' אברהם דנציג, מחבר ה"חיי אדם" וה"חכמת שלמה". במקרים של מחלוקות בין פוסקים אלו פסק גאנצפריד לפי דעת הרוב. בימינו, ה"משנה ברורה" תפסה את מקום ה"קיצור שולחן ערוך" כמעט לחלוטין, וה"חיי אדם" ו"ערוך השולחן" הינם הסמכויות המרכזיות בנושאי חיי היום-יום בקרב יהודים אשכנזיים.
heShortDesc: ספר הלכה ידוע שפורסם בשנת 1864. מתמצת ומנגיש את ההלכות הרלוונטיות לחיי היום-יום מתוך השולחן ערוך.

title: תשובות רפואיות
enDesc: Care of the Critically Ill is a 20th-century work that translates and explains more than a dozen of Rav (“Rabbi”) Moshe Feinstein’s responsa on caring for the critically ill, written by Rav Moshe’s student and son-in-law, Rabbi Moshe Tendler. Including both responsa published in Rabbi Feinstein’s “Iggrot Moshe” as well as previously unpublished responsa, the work addresses issues like the halakhic approach to brain death and the factor of “quality of life” when deciding whether to keep terminally ill patients on life support. It also includes a biography of Rav Moshe as well as an essay co-authored by Dr. Fred Rosner about quality and sanctity of life. The release and digitization of this book was kindly sponsored by The Applebaum Foundation.
enShortDesc: 20th-century translations of Rav Moshe Feinstein’s responsa on care of the critically ill.
heDesc: תהליך הדיגיטציה של ספר זה והנגשתו בחסות קרן אפלבאום.
heShortDesc: תרגום לאנגלית של מבחר תשובות של הרב משה פיינשטיין העוסקות בטיפול בחולה אנוש, חובר במאה ה-20.

title: שלח תשלח
enDesc: Shaleach Teshalech is a contemporary work that explores the commandment of Shiluach HaKen, sending away a mother bird before taking her young or her eggs. The work is in three parts: the first consists of legal analysis, incorporating the rulings of Rabbi Yosef Shalom Elyashiv and Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky. The second is called the aggadic part, analyzing the mitzvah’s essence, reasons, and rewards. The third is a practical guide for observing this commandment and other laws relating to birds.
enShortDesc: 21st-century work on the commandment to send away a mother bird before taking her young or her eggs.

title: גדר עולם
enDesc: Geder Olam is a treatise on modesty written by Rabbi Yisrael Meir HaKohen Kagan (known as the Chafetz Chaim after his work by that name), motivated by what he perceived as loosening standards of modesty, in dress and conduct, in contemporary religious society. Most of the work’s eight chapters focus on head-coverings for married women, but the importance, impact, and challenges of modesty in other realms are discussed as well, including a strong admonition against mixed-gender dancing.
enShortDesc: Late 19th-century work on the importance of modesty, written by Rabbi Yisrael Meir Kagan (the Chafetz Chaim).

title: חפץ חיים
enDesc: The Chafetz Chaim (“Desirer of Life,” a reference to Psalms 34:19) is the first legal work that comprehensively organizes the laws of proper speech, authored in the 20th century by Rabbi Yisrael Meir HaKohen Kagan (who later became known as the Chafetz Chaim). It draws on sources from the Torah, Talmud, and early commentators to address the details of lashon hara (evil speech) and rechilut (gossip), and is considered the authoritative work on these subjects. The text consists of two parts: Mekor Chaim (Source of Life), the legal text, and Be’er Mayim Chaim (Well of Living Water), footnotes containing elaborations and legal arguments. It is commonly printed together with Shemirat HaLashon (Guarding of the Tongue), an ethical treatise on proper speech.
enShortDesc: First work to exclusively address the laws of proper speech, written in the 20th century.
heShortDesc: החיבור הראשון המתמקד באופן בלעדי בדיני לשון הרע ורכילות ומסדר אותם באופן מקיף. נכתב במאה ה-20.

title: קסת הסופר
enDesc: Keset HaSofer (“The Inkstand of the Scribe״) is a legal handbook for scribes and the first work written by Rabbi Shlomo Ganzfried (the author of the Kitzur Shulchan Arukh). It includes the laws of writing Torah scrolls, mezuzot, tefillin, and Megilat Esther. In the work’s introduction, Rabbi Ganzfried explains that he wrote the book at nights while working as a wine merchant during the days. He writes that he was motivated to compile the book after noticing widespread ignorance on the laws of scribal writing, in part due to the lack of a centralized work exclusively addressing them. Keset HaSofer is still considered an essential guide for scribes.
enShortDesc: 19th-century work on the laws of scribal writing by the author of the Kitzur Shulchan Arukh.
heDesc: הלכות ספרות (כתיבת ספר תורה, תפלין ומזוזות) מבעל ה"קיצור שלחן ערוך".
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-19 של מחבר הקיצור שולחן ערוך העוסק בהלכות כתיבת סת"ם.

title: שערי אפרים
enDesc: Sha’arei Ephraim is a practical guide to the laws of public Torah reading by Rabbi Ephraim Zalman Margoliot, a respected halakhic authority of 18th–19th-century Galicia. The work is intended to facilitate study by community rabbis, who the author stresses should strive for full expertise in all areas of practical Jewish law, and to serve as a quick reference when a question arises during services and requires an immediate answer. It has become a widely accepted and relied-upon text, with many editions printed over the years, including translations and supplementary material by later scholars.
enShortDesc: Early 19th-century work on the laws of Torah reading, by Rabbi Ephraim Zalman Margoliot.

title: סדר היום
enDesc: Seder HaYom, meaning “Order of the Day,” was written by Rabbi Moshe ben Machir, a 16th-century halakhist and kabbalist of the Safed region. The book lays out a daily program of prayer and other behaviors, including  holiday rituals, Torah study, and interpersonal commandments such as visiting the sick, and is intended to guide the average individual toward the best use of time throughout each day and year, with the fundamental goal of fulfilling God’s will. The work includes commentary and instructions regarding performance as well as accompanying devotions. It is the earliest source of several customs, most notably the popular Modeh Ani prayer, an expression of gratitude recited immediately upon awakening each day.
enShortDesc: 16th-century legal and kabbalistic work by Rabbi Moshe ben Machir that guides daily and yearly observances.

title: עין התכלת
enDesc: Ein HaTekhelet is a work by the Radziner Rebbe (Rabbi Gershon Henoch Leiner) responding to questions and criticisms of his treatise “Treasures Hidden in the Sand,” in which he advocated searching for the source of tekhelet. Ein HaTekhelet was published after the Radziner Rebbe’s death.
enShortDesc: The Radziner Rebbe’s response to criticism of his treatise, “Treasures Hidden in the Sand.”
heDesc: תגובתו של רבי גרשון חנוך העניך ליינר (האדמו"ר השלישי של חסידות איזביצה-ראדזין) לביקורת על חיבורו  'שפוני טמוני חול'.
heShortDesc: תגובתו של רבי גרשון חנוך העניך ליינר (האדמו"ר השלישי של חסידות איזביצה-ראדזין) לביקורת על חיבורו  'שפוני טמוני חול'.

title: גבורת אנשים
enDesc: Gevurat Anashim is a work of the Shach (Rabbi Shabbatai ben Meir HaKohen, know for the acronym of his commentary on the Yoreh De’ah section of the Shulchan Arukh, the “Siftei Kohen”) on Shulchan Arukh, Even HaEzer, section 154:7. The section discusses a case in which a woman wants her husband to issue her a get (writ of divorce) on the basis that he lacks “the strength of men” (“gevurat anashim”) to perform sexually. In his introduction, the Shach writes that he was unsatisfied with the treatment of the subject in the Shulchan Arukh and commentators and therefore felt compelled to write his own work.
enShortDesc: 17th-century work about a case in which a woman wants a divorce due to sexual dysfunction.
heDesc: חובר על ידי ר' שבתי הכהן (בעל הש"ך). עוסק בנסיבות ובתנאים שבהם ניתן לאלץ גבר להעניק גט לאשתו.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-17 העוסק במקרה של אישה שמבקשת להתגרש מבעלה בשל בעיות ביחסי אישות.
heDescNew: מאוקסס (XXXXXX) מנטפרי

title: הלכות תלמוד תורה
enDesc: Hilchot Talmud Torah is a short treatise on the laws of Torah study by Rabbi Shneur Zalman of Liadi, founder and first rebbe of the Chabad branch of chasidic Judaism. It was the first work he published and was later included in his code of Jewish law, the Shulchan Arukh HaRav.
enShortDesc: 18th-century treatise on the laws of Torah study by the founder of the Chabad movement.
heShortDesc: מסה מן המאה ה-18 על הלכות תלמוד תורה שחובר על ידי מייסד חסידות חב"ד.

title: נהר מצרים
enDesc: Nehar Mitzrayim (“The River of Egypt”) is an early 20th-century work of laws and customs followed by Egyptian Jewry, by the former chief rabbi of Cairo, Rabbi Raphael Aharon ben Shimon. It follows the order of the Shulchan Arukh, but omits financial laws covered in the Choshen Mishpat section of the Shulchan Arukh because Egyptian Jews followed secular authorities on financial matters. The work incorporates a wide range of earlier sources and extensively addresses social, legal, and technological issues facing the community. It often describes commonly accepted practices, like drinking coffee before morning prayers (when generally, eating before prayers is considered forbidden), examining the practices in light of earlier halakhic sources and ben Shimon’s own reasoning.
enShortDesc: 20th-century work of laws and customs followed by Egyptian Jewry, by the chief rabbi of Cairo.
heDesc: אוסף של מנהגי מצרים ותקנותיה, נכתב ע"י רב רפאל אהרן בן שמעון, שהיה רבה הראשי של קהיר במצרים.
heShortDesc: אוסף מנהגים ותקנות של יהודי מצרים. חובר על ידי הרב הראשי של קהיר במאה ה-20.

title: מאמר שפוני טמוני חול
enDesc: Treasures Hidden in the Sand (a reference to Deuteronomy 33:19) is a 19th-century thesis arguing for the possibility of discovering the source of tekhelet, a dye that the Bible instructs to use in the High Priest’s clothing, the tapestry in the Mishkan (Tabernacle), and tzitzit (fringes affixed to four-cornered garments). The Tosefta (Menachot 9:6) states that tekhelet comes from the secretion of a sea-creature called the chilazon, but the identity of the chilazon was lost since early medieval times and wearing tekhelet fell out of practice. “Treasures” addresses and refutes potential objections to a modern-day search for the chilazon, and describes the signs of the chilazon as described in rabbinic literature. It is considered an essential source on the topic.
enShortDesc: 19th-century thesis advocating for the search for the source of tekhelet, a dye used in tzitzit.
heDesc: מאמר מאת הרב גרשון חנוך ליינר, האדמו"ר מראדזין (המכונה "בעל התכלת"), המסכם כי "דיונון הרוקחים" (שם מדעי: Sepia officinalis) עונה על קריטריונים רבים של התכלת למצוות ציצית.
heShortDesc: מסה מן המאה ה-19 שעוסקת במחקר מקורו של צבע התכלת, המשמש לצביעת פתיל צמר ('פתיל תכלת') בציצית.

title: טעמי המנהגים
enDesc: Ta'amei HaMinhagim U’Mekorei HaDinim (“Reasons for the Customs and Sources of the Laws”) by Rabbi Avraham Yitzchak Sperling explains the origins and reasons for over a thousand Jewish customs. The work includes practices unique to certain communities, including, for example, different chasidic communities. Immediately popular, it was revised and expanded five times by the author and has been published many times since. His grandson, Rabbi Moshe Sperling, published an edition combining the core work and shorter supplements by the author, alongside new material and indexes.
enShortDesc: A work of explanations of many different Jewish customs and practices.

title: כף אחת
enDesc: Kaf Achat (“One Ladle,” a reference to Numbers 7) is a collection of prayers and confessions to be recited under various circumstances, like when searching for a spouse or when worried about business transactions. It is part of Avodat HaKodesh (“Work that is Holy”), a compilation of seven short works of law, custom, and ethics written in the late 18th century by Rabbi Chaim Yosef David Azoulai (known as the “Chida” for his acronym). Avodat HaKodesh incorporates talmudic, rabbinic, and kabbalistic teachings, translating them into practical instructions for a proper and holy life. The first Hebrew book to be printed in Jerusalem, it has since been published in more than a hundred editions.
enShortDesc: Prayers and confessions for various circumstances, like when scared or worried.
heShortDesc: תפילות ווידויים למצבים אנושיים שונים, כמו מצבי דאגה וחרדה.

title: צפורן שמיר
enDesc: Tziporen Shamir (“The Point of a Diamond,” a reference to Jeremiah 17:1) addresses prayer and daily conduct, and is part of Avodat HaKodesh (“Work that is Holy”), a compilation of seven short works of law, custom, and ethics written in the late 18th century by Rabbi Chaim Yosef David Azoulai (known as the “Chida” for his acronym). The work incorporates talmudic, rabbinic, and kabbalistic teachings, translating them into practical instructions for a proper and holy life. The first Hebrew book to be printed in Jerusalem, Avodat HaKodesh has since been published in more than a hundred editions.
enShortDesc: Instructions for prayer and daily conduct.

title: מורה באצבע
enDesc: Moreh BeEtzba (“Instructing with a Finger”) addresses proper conduct and customs, including recommendations like not to eat too much at night, to refrain from anger, and to learn Torah immediately after praying. It is part of Avodat HaKodesh (“Work that is Holy”), a compilation of seven short works of law, custom, and ethics written in the late 18th century by Rabbi Chaim Yosef David Azoulai (known as the “Chida” for his acronym). Avodat HaKodesh incorporates talmudic, rabbinic, and kabbalistic teachings, translating them into practical instructions for a proper and holy life. The first Hebrew book to be printed in Jerusalem, it has since been published in more than a hundred editions.
enShortDesc: Proper conduct and customs for everyday, Shabbat, and holidays.

title: שומר ישראל
enDesc: Shomer Yisrael (“Guardian of Israel,” a reference to Psalms 121:4) is a collection of prayers for protection from both physical and spiritual danger, like the Yetzer HaRa (“Evil Inclination”). Avodat HaKodesh incorporates talmudic, rabbinic, and kabbalistic teachings, translating them into practical instructions for a proper and holy life. heShortDesc: תפילות להגנה מפני סכנות פיסיות או סכנות רוחניות כמו עין הרע.

title: יוסף בסדר

Avodat HaKodesh incorporates talmudic, rabbinic, and kabbalistic teachings, translating them into practical instructions for a proper and holy life. enShortDesc: Prayers for various circumstances, like after miraculous events or before Torah study at night.

title: קשר גודל
enDesc: Kesher Gudal (“Thumb Joint,” a reference to Menachot 42a) discusses the laws of tefillin, tzitzit, and prayer, and is part of Avodat HaKodesh (“Work that is Holy”), a compilation of seven short works of law, custom, and ethics written in the late 18th century by Rabbi Chaim Yosef David Azoulai (known as the “Chida” for his acronym). Avodat HaKodesh incorporates talmudic, rabbinic, and kabbalistic teachings, translating them into practical instructions for a proper and holy life. title: מעשה רב
enDesc: Maaseh Rav (“The Story/Practice of the Rabbi”) is a work detailing the personal legal practices and customs of the 18th-century rabbinic leader, the Vilna Gaon (Rabbi Eliyahu ben Shlomo Zalman, also referred to as the “Gra”), written by his student, Rabbi Sa’adya and edited by Rabbi Yissachar Dov Ber ben Tanchum. The work is considered a most reliable source of the Gaon’s legal opinions, and is quoted in later works like the Mishnah Berurah. It has been printed in dozens of editions.
enShortDesc: Work detailing the personal legal practices of the 18th-century rabbinic leader, the Vilna Gaon.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-18 המתאר הנהגות בתחום ההלכה וחיי היום-יום של הגאון מוילנא.

title: שמלה חדשה
enDesc: Simla Chadasha (“New Dress”) is an 18th-century compilation of the laws of shechita (ritual slaughter) by Rabbi Alexander Sender Schorr, who is often referred to as the Simla Chadasha. Based heavily on the relevant sections in the Shulchan Arukh, the work briefly presents laws, explanations, and sources, and is printed together with an extensive legal commentary by the author called Tevuot Shor. The Simla Chadasha is considered the definitive Ashkenazic work on shechita, and it is standard for prospective Ashkenazi shochtim (ritual slaughterers) to be tested on the work’s contents. The work has been published well over a hundred times.
enShortDesc: 18th-century work on ritual slaughter, considered the definitive Ashkenazic work on the topic.
heDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-18 שנחשב למדריך ההלכתי האשכנזי המובהק על הלכות שחיטה וטרפות.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-18 שנחשב למדריך ההלכתי האשכנזי המובהק על הלכות שחיטה וטרפות.

title: מטה אפרים
enDesc: Mateh Ephraim (“The Staff of Ephraim”) is a 19th-century compendium of laws and customs of the period from the beginning of the month of Elul and through Rosh Hashana, Yom Kippur, and the festival of Sukkot, as well as the laws pertaining to the orphan's Kaddish. It is often printed together with the commentary of the author, Elef l’Mateh. Considered an essential legal text on the high holidays, it has been printed in dozens of editions and has inspired much commentary.
enShortDesc: 19th-century compendium of laws and customs of the High Holidays and the festival of Sukkot.
heDesc: הלכות ומנהגים הנהוגים מראש חודש אלול עד אחר יום כיפור וקצת מדיני סוכות לפי סדר סימני השלחן ערוך. גם נכלל בו דיני קדיש יתום.
heShortDesc: אוסף מן המאה ה-19 של הלכות ומנהגי הימים הנוראים וחג הסוכות.

title: פתיל תכלת
enDesc: Ptil Tekhelet is the Radziner Rebbe (Rabbi Gershon Henoch Leiner)’s elaboration upon his treatise “Treasures Hidden in the Sand.” Ptil Tekhelet explains the Rebbe’s conclusion that the chilazon sea-creature described in rabbinic literature is the common cuttlefish, details the process of extracting the dye, and presents the laws of incorporating tekhelet into tzitzit (fringes affixed to four-cornered garments).
enShortDesc: The Radziner Rebbe’s elaboration upon “Treasures Hidden in the Sand,” his treatise on tekhelet.
heShortDesc: הרחבה של רבי גרשון חנוך העניך ליינר  לספרו 'שפוני טמוני חול', העוסק במצוות פתיל תכלת בציצית.

title: קול יעקב על שולחן ערוך
enDesc: Kol Yaakov is a collection of laws related to the scribing of holy texts, such as tefillin, mezuzot, Torah scrolls, and megillot. Written in Baghdad around the beginning of the 20th century by Rabbi Yaakov Chaim Sofer, it is organized according to the Shulchan Arukh to facilitate cross-referencing, and includes specific traditions of the Baghdad community, in addition to other widespread details of Jewish law. A second edition was printed in the author’s lifetime with additional material on the production of tefillin and mezuzot, such as kabbalistic kavanot (intentions) to accompany each stage of the scribal process.
enShortDesc: Early 20th-century collection of laws related to scribal practice.

heAuthors: אריה לייב בן יוסף הכהן הלר
title: שב שמעתתא
enDesc: The Shev Shmateta (“Seven Passages” in Aramaic)  is an 18th-century work on cases of doubt in the Talmud by the Ketzot (Rabbi Aryeh Leib HaKohen Heller). The work isolates the talmudic principles that relate to cases of doubt, testing each principle against a series of talmudic passages to clarify and elucidate the nature of the principle. The work includes an extensive theological introduction explaining the author’s outlook on Judaism, in which he explains his conviction that wrestling with talmudic analysis is the highest form of religious endeavor. The Shev Shmat’ta is considered a classic work in yeshivot, serving as a cornerstone of a popular analytic method of Talmud study.
enShortDesc: 18th-century work on cases of doubt in the Talmud, considered a classic of yeshiva study.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-18, העוסק בשבע סוגיות הלכתיות סבוכות בתלמוד. נחשב לקלאסיקה בלימוד ישיבתי.
heDescNew: חיבור מן המאה ה-18, העוסק בשבע סוגיות הלכתיות סבוכות בתלמוד. נחשב לספר יסוד בלימוד ישיבתי.

title: אהבת חסד
enDesc: Ahavat Chesed is a 19th-century work on performing acts of loving-kindness by Rabbi Yisrael Meir HaKohen Kagan, author of the Mishnah Berurah and the Chafetz Chaim. It details how to properly give loans to the needy, perform hospitality, celebrate with a bride and groom, visit the sick, write a will, comfort the mourning, and bury the dead. It also incorporates talmudic stories and teachings about the greatness of chesed. The work is printed with the Netiv Chesed, an elaborating commentary written by the author.
enShortDesc: 19th-century work on acts of kindness, such as giving loans to the needy and visiting the sick.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-19 העוסק במעשי חסד, כגון מתן הלוואות לנזקקים וביקור חולים.

Written over a period of ten years, the work systematically categorizes and clearly explains all aspects of Jewish observance, including those applicable only in Temple times.

title: קונטרס זיקה
enDesc: Kuntres Zikah, by Rabbi Meir Simcha of Dvinsk, was originally printed as part of his Ohr Sameach commentary on Rambam’s Mishneh Torah. It analyzes detailed laws of levirate marriage, in particular the “zikah,” or bond, that takes effect between a widow and the brother of her childless husband upon her husband’s death. Understanding the nature of this bond impacts questions such as whether there is a familial relationship established between the brother and the widow’s relatives if she dies before the levirate marriage takes place.
enShortDesc: Late 19th-century work on the laws of levirate marriage by Rabbi Meir Simcha of Dvinsk, originally and often printed as part of his Ohr Sameach commentary on Maimonides’ Mishneh Torah.

enTitle: Kessef Mishneh on Mishneh Torah, Reading the Shema
enDesc: Kessef Mishneh is a commentary on Rambam’s Mishneh Torah, written by Joseph Karo, and published during his lifetime. In the introduction to this work, the author writes that his goal was to cite the source of each law, and to defend the Rambam from Raavad's arguments.
heDesc: "כסף משנה" הוא פירוש למשנה תורה של הרמב"ם, שנכתב על ידי ר' יוסף קארו, ונדפס בחייו בוונציה, 1574-1575. בהקדמתו כותב המחבר שמטרות הספר הן לציין את מקורותיו של הרמב"ם בכל הלכה, ולהשיב לראב"ד ולרמ"ך בהשגותיהם על רמב"ם.

title: מעשה רקח על הלכות תפילה וברכת כהנים
enTitle: Maaseh Rokeach on Prayer and the Priestly Blessing
enDesc: Commentary to Rambam's Mishneh Torah by R' Mas'ud Hai Rokach. Also included are novellae of earlier commentators that had not been previously published, including those of Rambam's son Avraham. The work was completed by the author's son-in-law R' Natan Adadi. The first part was published by the author in Venice in 1742-1743. Volume 2 was published by his great-grandson Abraham Hayyim Adadi, in Livorno in 1862. Volume 3 was published in Livorno in 1863 by his great-great-grandson, Jacob Rakkah. Volume 4 was published in Jerusalem in 1964 by Rabbi Shmuel Akiva Yaffe-Schlesinger.
heDesc: פירוש על משנה תורה להרמב"ם מהרב מסעוד חי רקח. בתחילת הספר הוסיף פירושים על הרמב"ם ממספר ראשונים, ובראשם ר' אברהם בן הרמב"ם. חידושי הרב רקח מגיעים עד לאמצע ספר קנין, ומשם ואילך יש חידושים של חתנו ר' נתן אדאדי מחבר הספר "נתן מאורות".

enDesc: Commentary to Rambam's Mishneh Torah by R' Mas'ud Hai Rokach. Also included are novellae of earlier commentators that had not been previously published, including those of Rambam's son Avraham. The work was completed by the author's son-in-law R' Natan Adadi. The first part was published by the author in Venice in 1742-1743. Volume 2 was published by his great-grandson Abraham Hayyim Adadi, in Livorno in 1862. Volume 3 was published in Livorno in 1863 by his great-great-grandson, Jacob Rakkah. Volume 4 was published in Jerusalem in 1964 by Rabbi Shmuel Akiva Yaffe-Schlesinger.

enDesc: Lechem Shamayim is a commentary on the Mishnah and on a section of Maimonides’ Mishneh Torah by Rabbi Yaakov Emden (known by his initials as Ya’avetz). It was the first of many works by Rabbi Emden, published before he established his own printing press. He introduces the work with apologies for presuming to contribute to existing Jewish scholarship despite his youth, and specifically for arguing with the highly regarded Tosafot Yom Tov commentary, which he notes was the only Mishnah commentary available to him.
enShortDesc: 18th-century commentary by Rabbi Yaakov Emden.

title: פסקי רקנאטי
enDesc: Piskei Recanati is a 14th-century legal work on a range of topics by Italian scholar Rabbi Menachem Recanati, known for his writings on kabbalah. The work consists mainly of compilations of earlier legal works and varies in style, with some sections consisting of two or three terse lines and others containing lengthy discourses with detailed analysis. It was first published in the 16th-century and subsequently reprinted in several editions. Later authorities frequently quote Piskei Recanati as an authoritative source.
enShortDesc: 14th-century work by Italian scholar Rabbi Menachem Recanati, known for his writings on kabbalah.

title: חכמת אדם
enDesc: Chokhmat Adam‎ ("The Wisdom of Man"), a sequel to Chayei Adam, is a code that discusses the laws in the Yoreh De'ah section of the Shulchan Aruch and some laws from the Even Ha'ezer and Choshen Mishpat sections. The work collects and sifts the material written in the two and a half centuries since the Shulchan Arukh’s publication, summarizing laws and adding conceptual explanations in language designed to be accessible for those not fully versed in rabbinic literature. An addendum called Binat Adam, often printed together with the work, includes further elaborations.
enShortDesc: Sequel to Chayei Adam covering dietary regulations and other assorted laws, published in 1812.
heDesc: קיצור הלכות מחלק יורה דעה בשו"ע, וקצת מחשן משפט ואבן העזר הנוגעים בחיי היום-יום.
heShortDesc: ספר המשך ל'חיי אדם' שפורסם בשנת 1812. עוסק בדיני כשרות ותחומים הלכתיים נוספים.

title: תורת הבית הארוך
enDesc: Torat HaBayit HaAroch (“The Long Laws of the House”) is a legal manual on ritual observances - like kashrut, niddah, and mikvah immersion - relevant for maintaining a Jewish home. The work reviews talmudic discussions and the positions of the Rashba’s predecessors, raises and refutes objections, and advances the Rashba’s own positions. The Re’ah, an old friend of the Rashba, wrote a critical commentary called the Bedek HaBayit. The Rashba then anonymously wrote the Mishmeret HaBayit, a defense against the Re’ah’s criticisms written in the third-person. Both commentaries are printed together with the Torat HaBayit, which is considered a critical legal text and is quoted often by later authorities.
enShortDesc: 13th-century legal manual on ritual observances like kashrut, niddah, and mikvah immersion.
heShortDesc: חיבור הלכתי של הרשב״א מן המאה ה-13 העוסק בהלכות כשרות, נידה ומקוואות.

title: כל בו
enDesc: Kol Bo (“Everything Within”) is a 13th or 14th-century legal work of unknown authorship that draws on earlier sources to address a wide range of topics. It does not appear to be arranged in any particular order or to follow a consistent style; some laws are stated briefly while others are discussed extensively. Legends, kabbalistic discourse, gematria, and responsa are at times interspersed with legal explanations. Siman 51 consists of commentary on the Passover Haggadah. Because of its varied nature, later works often refer to the book as “Sefer haLikkutim,” or “Book of Assorted Material.”
enShortDesc: 13th or 14th-century anonymous work with legal rulings and occasional explanations.
heDesc: ספר הלכה מתקופת הראשונים המכיל דינים ומנהגים לכל השנה. שם המחבר אינו ידוע, ויש משערים שהוא מהדורא ראשונית או קיצור של הספר "ארחות חיים" של ר' אהרן מלוניל.
heShortDesc: חיבור אנונימי מן המאה ה-13 או 14 המאגד פסקי הלכה ומנהגים. מכיל את אחד הפירושים המוקדמים ביותר להגדה של פסח.

title: אור זרוע
enDesc: Ohr Zarua (“Light is Sown,” a reference to Psalms 97:11) is a 13th-century compilation tracing the development of laws from talmudic passages. It is an important source preserving early medieval legal opinions, particularly those of the Tosafists. It is also considered a valuable resource for the history of medieval European Jewish communities, since its legal questions often shed light on historical realities. Although it was not widely circulated and only began to be published in the 19th century, several legal authorities had access to the work, and its positions are quoted often in the Beit Yosef and Darkei Moshe.
enShortDesc: 13th-century compilation tracing the development of laws from talmudic passages.
heShortDesc: אוסף הלכתי מן המאה ה-13 העוקב אחר התפתחות ההלכה החל מן המקור התלמודי, ומשמר מסורות הלכתיות חשובות.

title: משפטי בדיקת הסכין לרבי יונה זצל
enDesc: Bedikat HaSakin (“Checking of the Knife”) is a 13th-century treatise on the process of checking the knife used for ritual slaughter and checking an animal for defects or injuries that would render it a terefah (an animal disqualified from being kosher because of defects or injuries), by Rabbeinu Yonah Gerondi. It was first printed in the 19th century in the back of Teshuvot HaGeonim.
enShortDesc: 13th-century work on checking the knife used for slaughter and checking animals for defects.
heDesc: מאמר הלכתי לרבינו יונה בענין שחיטה כשירה.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-13 העוסק בסכין השחיטה ובבדיקת מומים בחיות הנשחטות.

title: ספר חסידים
enDesc: Sefer Chasidim (“Book of the Pious”) is an ethical and legal guide to everyday life and a foundational text of Chasidei Ashkenaz, a mystical and ascetic movement that flourished in Germany during the 12th and 13th centuries. The work teaches the righteous how to dress, speak, pray, work, sleep, interact with gentile neighbors, and make life-decisions, like whom to marry and where to live. It puts an emphasis on avoiding honor, wealth, physical pleasure, and extramarital sex, and its legal rulings are generally stringent. Given the ample attention the work devotes to realistic details, it is considered a critical source for studying Jewish civilization in medieval Germany.
enShortDesc: Ethical and legal guide to everyday life; foundational work of medieval German pietists.
heShortDesc: מדריך בענייני הלכה ומוסר להתנהלות ראויה בחיי היום-יום. חיבור יסודי בקרב חסידי אשכנז בימי הביניים.

title: סלע המחלקות על בעלי הנפש
enDesc: Sela HaMachlakot, a Hebrew phrase taken from I Samuel 23:28, is the title that Rabbi Zerachiah HaLevi gave his commentaries on two of Ra’avad’s works: one about Mishnah Tractate Kinnim, which discusses bird-offerings, and the other, Ra’avad’s Ba’alei HaNefesh, which discusses laws related to menstruation and sexual conduct. The latter is known as Rabbi Zerachiah HaLevi’s Hasagot (Glosses) and is heavily critical of the Ra’avad’s work. The author’s poetic introduction was added based on manuscript evidence in a recent edition by Yosef Qafiḥ.
enShortDesc: 12th-century commentary more often known as the Hasagot (Glosses) of Rabbi Zerachiah HaLevi on the Ra’avad’s Ba’alei HaNefesh.

title: לקט יושר
enDesc: Leket Yosher is a 15th-century work by Rabbi Yosef ben Moshe that records the customs and legal opinions of his teacher, Rabbi Yisrael Isserlein. The work also includes a biography of Isserlein and several of his responsa. In an introduction, the author writes that he came to compile the book after receiving questions about his teacher’s opinions on legal matters while traveling. When Rabbi Yosef was not able to easily answer these questions, he realized that it would be valuable to record his teacher’s practices and opinions so that others could easily learn from them. Leket Yosher was first published from manuscript in 1903.
enShortDesc: 15th-century work recording the customs and legal opinions of Rabbi Yisrael Isserlein.

title: שער המים הקצר
enDesc: Sha’ar HaMayim HaKatzar is the Rashba’s abridgement of his Sha’ar HaMayim HaArokh, a compilation of laws about the mikvah (ritual bath). Sha’ar HaMayim HaArokh presents rulings, explanation, and analysis of topics like valid sources of water for a mikvah and conditions that disqualify a mikvah. Sha’ar HaMayim HaKatzar presents only the actual laws. These works are found in the back of some manuscripts of the Rashba’s Torat haBayit and are quoted by commentators like the Rivash, the Tashbetz and the Beit Yosef.
enShortDesc: The Rashba’s abridgement of his Sha’ar HaMayim HaArokh.
heShortDesc: מהדורה קצרה של החיבור 'שער המים הארוך' של הרשב"א.

title: תשבץ קטן
enDesc: Tashbetz Katan is a 13th-century collection of teachings and practices of the Maharam of Rothenberg. When the Maharam was imprisoned after attempting to flee Germany, his student Rabbi Shimshon ben Tzadok visited him. During these visits, Rabbi Shimshon recorded the Maharam’s legal opinions, personal practices, and Torah insights, adding in his own occasional commentary as well. 13th-century scholar Rabbenu Peretz later added notes to the text, which appear in brackets and begin with the word “mihu” (“however”).
enShortDesc: 13th-century collection of teaching and practices of the Maharam of Rothenburg.

title: הלכות נדה לרמבן
enDesc: Hilkhot Niddah of the Ramban (Rabbi Moshe ben Nachman) consists of 9 chapters, each made up of short paragraphs explaining the definitions and practical applications of different aspects of the laws of niddah (a woman in her menstrual cycle or experiencing particular discharges). The author explains in his introduction that he wrote this short practical guide only upon request, after initially protesting that there were already sufficient books on the subject, such as the Ra’avad’s Ba’alei HaNefesh. His rulings are frequently quoted by later legal authorities, though many did not have access to this work until after its first printing in 1741, as part of a collection entitled Todat Shelamim. The work has been reprinted numerous times, often alongside Ba’alei HaNefesh (which was also included in Todat Shelamim).
enShortDesc: 13th-century work by the Ramban on the practical application of the laws of niddah (a woman in her menstrual cycle or experiencing particular discharges).

title: עבודת הקדש
enDesc: Avodat HaKodesh (“Sacred Work”) is a 13th-century compilation of laws relating to Shabbat and holidays. Like the Torat HaBayit, the other legal treatise written by the Rashba, the Avodat HaKodesh originally appeared in two versions, one long and the other abridged. The long version is not extant; this is the abridged version. It consists of two main sections. The first mainly addresses eruvin, or enclosures that legally expand the areas in which one can carry and travel on Shabbat. The second addresses permitted preparation of food on holidays, among other topics.
enShortDesc: 13th-century compilation of laws relating to Shabbat and holidays.
heShortDesc: אוסף הלכות שבת ויום טוב מן המאה ה-13.

title: איסור והיתר לרשי
enDesc: Issur VeHeter LeRashi is an incomplete composition of rulings and responsa attributed to Rashi. Though its title implies that it addresses dietary laws (“Issur VeHeter'' literally means “forbidden and permitted” and is the term often used to refer to dietary laws), the work covers a range of topics, with the first third addressing holidays. The work is one of several works - Machzor Vitri being another notable one - compiled after Rashi’s death in an attempt to collect his legal positions.
enShortDesc: Incomplete composition of rulings and responsa on a variety of topics, attributed to Rashi.
heDesc: שו"ת מיוחסות לרש"י
heShortDesc: שו"ת ופסקי הלכה המיוחסים לרש"י ועוסקים במבחר סוגיות הלכתיות.

title: שאילתות דרב אחאי גאון
enDesc: Sheiltot d’Rav Achai Gaon (“Questions of Rabbi Achai Gaon”) is an Aramaic collection of legal sermons and the first extant rabbinic work written after the Talmud’s completion. Unique in its structure, it is not arranged by subject matter or according to the Talmud, but rather according to the order of the Torah. Each sheilta (question) generally follows the same form, opening with a general introduction to a commandment, followed by a legal question related to the commandment, followed by a narrative or ethical section, and ending with an answer to the legal question. The work was considered a critical and highly authoritative work for subsequent legal authorities.
enShortDesc: First known rabbinic book written after the Talmud’s completion, with legal sermons on the Torah.
heDesc: הספר ההלכתי הראשון שנתחבר לאחר חתימת התלמוד.
heShortDesc: אוסף של דרשות הלכתיות על פרשת השבוע. ידוע כספר ההלכה הראשון שנכתב לאחר חתימת התלמוד.

title: שלחן של ארבע
enDesc: Sיulchan shel Arba (“Table of Four,” a title which the author chose for four reasons that he details in the introduction) is a 14th-century handbook meant to be studied at meals, written by the preacher, Torah commentator, and kabbalist Rabbenu Bachya ben Asher. It consists of four chapters; the first discusses the laws pertaining to meals, like handwashing and blessings on food, the second and third describe proper spiritual intentions and ethical rules of conduct during mealtime, and the fourth describes the banquet of the righteous that will take place in the Messianic era.
enShortDesc: 14th-century handbook on laws and spiritual aspects of eating, meant to be studied at meals.
heDesc: ספרו של רבינו בחיי שעוסק בעניני אכילה. הספר מחולק לארבעה שערים: שער הראשון מבאר הדינים הנוגעים בשעת הסעודה ועניני ברכות הנהנין, שערים שני ושלישי מכיל עניני מוסר והנהגה הנכונה בשעת האכילה, והשער הרביעי עוסק בענין סעודת הצדיקים העתידה להיערך בזמן הגאולה.
heShortDesc: מדריך שנכתב במאה ה-14 על הלכות סעודה ועל ההיבטים הרוחניים של האכילה. נועד ללימוד במהלך הסעודה.

title: גנזי מצרים, הלכות ספר תורה
enDesc: Hilchot Sefer Torah, also called Ginzei Mitzrayim, is a medieval work on the laws of writing a Torah scroll and other sanctified books. First published from a Cairo genizah manuscript by Elchanan Adler in 1897, it was originally attributed to early 12th-century scholar Rabbi Yehuda ben Barzilai of Barcelona. Later scholars cast aspersions on that attribution, suggesting alternative authors such as 13th-century Iraqi scholar Rabbi Joseph Rosh Haseder.
enShortDesc: 12th-century work on the laws of writing a Torah scroll.

title: איסור והיתר הארוך
enDesc: Issur VeHeter HaArokh is a 15th-century composition on dietary laws (referred to as “issur v’heter,” which translates as “forbidden and permitted”). The author was an Ashkenazi legal authority and a contemporary of the Trumat HaDeshen, but his exact identity is a matter of debate. Issur VeHeter HaArokh was a central source upon which Rav Moshe Isserles (the Rema) relied in his legal rulings.
enShortDesc: 15th-century composition on dietary laws by an Ashkenazi legal authority.
heDesc: "איסור והיתר הארוך", הידוע גם בראשי התבות או"ה, הוא ספר הלכה שנכתב בגרמניה במאה ה־15. זהות מחבר הספר אינה ידועה. כינויו – ”הארוך” – בא להבחין בינו ובין ספרו של רבי יצחק מדורא, ”שערי דורא”, הנקרא גם ”איסור והיתר הקצר”. הספר עוסק בהלכות איסור והיתר, כלומר בהלכות הדברים המותרים והאסורים באכילה, ובנוסף בדיני טבילת כלים ופיקוח נפש. זהות מחבר הספר אמנם שנויה במחלוקת, אך ידוע כי היה מחכמי חבל הריין שבגרמניה ושהיה בן זמנו של רבי ישראל איסרלין, המכונה ”תרומת הדשן”. הספר הוא אחד המקורות המרכזיים ביותר עליהם הסתמך הרמ"א בפסיקותיו בחלק יורה דעה. חשיבותן של פסיקות הספר, שאינן מופיעות בשולחן ערוך, היו אחד ממניעיו לחיבור ”דרכי משה” - פירושו של הרמ"א על הטור.
heShortDesc: "איסור והיתר הארוך" הוא ספר הלכה שנכתב בגרמניה במאה ה־15, שזהות מחברו אינה ידועה. הספר עוסק בהלכות כשרות, דיני טבילת כלים ופיקוח נפש.

title: ספר האורה
enDesc: Sefer HaOrah is a collection of legal material attributed to Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo ben Yitzchak) and is part of a body of literature known as Sifrei DeVei Rashi (Works of the School of Rashi), compiled by Rashi’s students. It also contains legal rulings of other authorities, such as Rabbi Yehuda of Barcelona (author of Sefer HaItim), and overlaps in content with other works from the school of Rashi as well. It was published in 1905 by Solomon Buber based on several variant manuscripts.
enShortDesc: Early medieval collection of material on a variety of topics of Jewish law, attributed primarily to Rashi and compiled by his students.

title: פסקי חלה
enDesc: Piskei Challah is a 13th-century short work by the Rashba (Rabbi Shlomo ben Avraham ibn Aderet) about separating challah, a portion of dough given to priests. Though printed only twice before the 20th century, several early commentators, like the Meiri, had access to manuscripts and quoted the work often.
enShortDesc: 13th-century work of the Rashba about separating challah, a portion of dough given to priests.
heShortDesc: חיבור שנכתב על ידי הרשב"א במאה ה-13 העוסק בהפרשת חלה.

title: האגור
enDesc: *Sefer HaAgur* is a 15th-century halakhic digest by Rabbi Jacob Landau, covering topics addressed in the Orach Chaim and Yoreh Deah sections of Rabbi Jacob ben Asher’s [Tur](https://www.sefaria.org/Tur?tab=contents). In his introduction, Landau writes that he wrote his book for his student, who was busy studying physics and metaphysics and did not have time to study Jewish law from its talmudic sources. Based primarily on the Tur, *Sefer HaAgur* presents a summary of existing opinions for each given law, a legal ruling, and a summary of the questions and cases raised in recent halakhic literature since the publication of the Tur. *Sefer HaAgur* was novel in its occasional incorporation of kabbalistic considerations into halakhic rulings. It was also the first published Hebrew book to contain *haskamot,” approbations from other rabbis.
enShortDesc: 15th-century halakhic digest by R. Jacob Landau
heDesc: 'ספר האגור' הוא ספר הלכה מהמאה ה-15 מאת רבי יעקב יעקב לנדא הסוקר את שיטות ההלכה השונות. הספר עוסק בנושאים שנידונו בחלקי 'אורח חיים' ו'יורה דעה' בספר 'ארבעה טורים' של רבי יעקב בן אשר, הידוע בשם 'הטור'. בהקדמתו כותב לנדא שכתב את ספרו עבור תלמידו שהיה עסוק בלימודי פיזיקה ומטאפיזיקה ולא הספיק ללמוד את ההלכה היהודית ממקורותיה התלמודיים. בהתבסס בעיקר על הטור, מציג 'ספר האגור' סיכום של הדעות השונות לגבי נושאים הלכתיים שונים ותמצית של שאלות ומקרים שהועלו בספרות ההלכתית העדכנית עד לזמנו מאז פרסום ה'טור'. 'ספר האגור' היה חדשני בשילוב חכמת הקבלה בפסיקת הלכה. ספר זה גם היה הספר העברי הראשון המודפס עם הסכמות של רבנים אחרים.
heShortDesc: ספר פסיקה וסקירה הלכתית מהמאה ה-15 מאת ר' יעקב יעקב לנדא

heAuthors: ר' צדקיה בן ר' אברהם הרופא
title: שבלי הלקט
enDesc: Shibbolei HaLeket is a 13th-century work of Jewish law by Italian scholar Tzedakia ben Avraham Anaw. It primarily covers topics discussed in the [Orach Chaim](https://www.sefaria.org/Shulchan_Arukh,_Orach_Chayim?tab=contents) section of the Shulchan Arukh and consists of legal rulings and analyses based in large part on three types of sources: geonic responsa, works from the beit midrash of Rashi, and works of [Isaiah di Trani](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/isaiah-dtrani). The book is a main source of law relied upon in the Orach Chaim section of the Tur, and is quoted in almost every chapter (siman) of the Beit Yosef there.
enShortDesc: 13th-century work by Italian scholar Tzedakia ben Avraham Anaw

title: דינא דגרמי
enDesc: Dina DeGarmei (“The Law of Those Who Cause,” a talmudic phrase) is a short 13th-century treatise by Ramban about the complex topic of indirect damages. In it, Nachmanides surveys the talmudic passages that address different forms of indirect damages as well as the positions of earlier authorities and advances his own argument about what factors render a person liable for indirect damage. Since the subject is addressed in the second chapter of tractate Bava Batra, the treatise is often printed as an appendix to the author’s commentary on the tractate. It is considered a central work on the topic and has inspired several commentaries.
enShortDesc: 13th-century short treatise about indirect damages by Ramban
heShortDesc: מסה קצרה שנכתבה על ידי הרמב"ן במאה ה-13, העוסקת בדיני נזקים עקיפים.

title: תורת הבית הקצר
enDesc: Torat HaBayit HaKatzar (“The Short Laws of the House”) is the Rashba’s abridgement of his Torat HaBayit HaArokh. Both works cover ritual observances relevant for maintaining a Jewish home, like kashrut, niddah, and mikvah immersion. Meant to serve as a guidebook, the Torat HaBayit HaKatzar focuses on practical law and omits the discussions and analyses that are characteristic of the longer version.
enShortDesc: Abridged version of Torat HaBayit HaArokh by the same author, focusing on practical law.
heShortDesc: מהדורה מקוצרת של 'תורת הבית הארוך' של הרשב"א, המתמקדת בהלכה למעשה.

title: תורת האדם
enDesc: *Torat HaAdam* is Ramban’s 13th-century work on the laws surrounding the end of life, including the treatment of a dying person on Shabbat, confession, burial, and mourning. The book was considered an essential source of authority, quoted often by medieval scholars and incorporated by Rabbi Jacob ben Asher and Rabbi Joseph Karo into their monumental codes, [Arba’ah Turim](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Halakhah/Tur) and [Shulchan Arukh](https://www.sefaria.org/texts/Halakhah/Shulchan%20Arukh), respectively. The title *Torat HaAdam* (likely a reference to II [Samuel 7:19](https://www.sefaria.org/II_Samuel.7.19?ven=Tanakh:_The_Holy_Scriptures,_published_by_JPS&lang=he)) is absent from the work’s manuscripts but appears on the title page of the first printed edition. Other medieval scholars also refer to the work by this title. The book includes a section entitled *Sha’ar HaGemul*, on reward and punishment, theodicy, heaven and hell, and the afterlife.
enShortDesc: 12th-century work by Ramban on laws of end of life, such as treatment of a dying person on Shabbat, confession, burial, and mourning
heDesc: 'תורת האדם' הוא חיבורו של הרמב"ן מהמאה ה-12 על הלכות הנוגעות לסוף החיים, לרבות טיפול באדם גוסס בשבת, וידוי, קבורה ואבל. הספר נחשב למקור סמכות חיוני, שצוטט לעתים קרובות על ידי חוקרי ימי הביניים ושולב על ידי רבי יעקב בן אשר ורבי יוסף קארו בחיבוריהם הגדולים, 'ארבע טורים' ו'שולחן ערוך', בהתאמה. הכותרת 'תורת האדם' (כנראה התייחסות לשמואל ב' ז, יט) נעדרת מכתבי היד של היצירה אך מופיעה בשער המהדורה המודפסת הראשונה. חכמים אחרים מימי הביניים מתייחסים גם הם ליצירה בכותרת זו. הספר כולל חלק שכותרתו 'שער הגמול', שעוסק ב'שכר ועונש', גן עדן וגיהנום והעולם הבא.
heShortDesc: חיבור מהמאה ה-12 מאת הרמב"ן על הלכות סוף החיים, כמו טיפול בגוסס בשבת, וידוי, קבורה ואבל.

title: ספר התרומה
enDesc: Sefer HaTerumah was written by the tosafist Barukh ben Isaac of Worms. The author presents concise statements of Jewish law on a variety of topics in a practical style that was innovative at the time and contributed to its popularity and influence, including a table of contents that summarizes each topic. Topics include kosher slaughter, Shabbat, marriage, and agricultural laws related to the land of Israel. Sefer HaTerumah is often cited as authoritative by later legal scholars.
enShortDesc: 13th-century summary of Jewish law related to various topics by Barukh ben Isaac of Worms and often quoted by later authorities

title: סדר טרוייש
enDesc: Seder Troyes is one of several works composed in the medieval period in order to preserve communal customs despite persecution and expulsions. Written by Menachem ben Yosef, a second-generation chazzan (prayer leader), and edited by his student, Eliezer ben Yehuda, it contains ten chapters explaining the structure and content of daily prayers as well as prayers recited on Shabbat, holidays, and other occasions. Its traditions likely reflect the rulings of Rashi, leading Torah scholar in Troyes in the 11th century.
enShortDesc: 13th-century record of prayer customs according to the traditions of the French city of Troyes.

title: אבודרהם
enDesc: The Sefer Abudarham is a popular 14th-century compilation of laws, customs, and commentary on the prayer book, named for its author, Rabbi David Abudarham. In his introduction, Abudarham explains that he was motivated to write the book because he felt that the masses were unequipped to understand the content of the prayers they muttered or the surrounding customs. The work draws on a wide array of earlier materials and incorporates commentary on the Passover Haggadah as well as a systematic explanation of the Hebrew calendar. It is considered a central text on prayer, published in many editions and quoted frequently in later works.
enShortDesc: Popular 14th-century compilation of laws, customs, and commentary on the prayer book.
heDesc: נקרא במקורו "חיבור על פירוש הברכות והתפילות", אבל נודע בשם מחברו "אבודרהם". כולל פירוש ומנהגים על סדר התפילה.
heShortDesc: אוסף הלכות, מנהגים, ופירושים לתפילה, מן המאה ה-14.

title: ספר המחכים
enDesc: Sefer HaMachkim is a summary and explanation of daily and holiday prayer services, including guidelines for prayer leaders. Written in the 13th century by Rabbi Natan ben Yehuda, it cites a number of earlier scholars, including the author’s father and great-grandfather, and is quoted frequently by later authorities. The author notes that he wrote it after being asked for an orderly guide to prayer, to better support the encounter with the divine.
enShortDesc: 13th-century guide to the order of prayers recited daily and on holidays, by Rabbi Natan ben Yehuda.

title: ספר הפרנס
enDesc: Sefer HaParnas is a 13th or 14th-century collection of traditions and rulings of Rabbi Meir of Rothenburg (known as the Maharam of Rothenburg), compiled by his student, Rabbi Moshe Parnas. The work was well-known and quoted often by German scholars in the 15th century, but was then lost and not published until the late 19th century.f Rothenburg.
enShortDesc: 13th or 14th-century collection of traditions and rulings of the Maharam of Rothenburg.
heDesc: ליקוט של פסקי הלכה ומנהגים של ר' מאיר מרוטנברג (מהר"ם), כפי שרשמם תלמידו ר' משה פרנס.
heShortDesc: אוסף מנהגים ופסקי הלכה המיוחסים למהר"ם מרוטנברג, חובר במאה ה-13 או 14 .

title: ספר המכריע
enDesc: Sefer HaMakhria is a 13th-century talmudic commentary written by the Italian tosafist Isaiah d'Trani, also known as Tosafot Rid (HaZaken) after the name of his best-known work. Sefer HaMakria contains 92 chapters of varying lengths, each of which cites a passage from the Talmud and then analyzes the passage and its legal ramifications, often in dialogue with explanations of other scholars. One of these is Rashi, often referred to by the author as HaMoreh.
enShortDesc: 13th-century talmudic commentary on select tractates, by the Italian tosafist Isaiah d'Trani, also known as Tosafot Rid.

title: אגרת השבת
enDesc: The Sabbath Epistle is a 12th-century polemical letter defending the traditional view that Shabbat begins at dusk, attributed to the biblical commentator Rabbi Abraham Ibn Ezra. In a preface, Ibn Ezra describes how he received a letter from Shabbat in a dream, instructing him to defend Shabbat. When he woke up, he discovered a commentary, presumably that of the Rashbam to Genesis 1:5, suggesting that a day in the Jewish calendar starts at dawn rather than the accepted view that a day begins at dusk. Realizing that this would lead to desecration of Shabbat, the Ibn Ezra set out to justify the traditional view. The work thus provides a general explanation of the Jewish calendar, incorporating astronomy and biblical interpretation.
enShortDesc: 12th-century polemical letter defending the traditional view that Shabbat begins at dusk.
heDesc: חיבור קטן מאבן עזרא, בו הוא מוכיח שיום השבת מתחיל מבערב, להוציא מדעת מי שטען שהלילה הולך אחר היום. כמו כן דן הספר בזמן תחילת החדש והשנה על פי תורה. המחבר כותב שהוא קיבל את תוכן הספר בדמות אגרת מהשבת בחלום הלילה.
heShortDesc: חיבור מן המאה ה-12 שבו מגן רבי אברהם אבן-עזרא על העמדה ההלכתית המסורתית, לפיה השבת מתחילה ביום שישי בערב.
heDescNew: חיבור מן המאה ה-12 שבו מגן רבי אברהם אבן-עזרא על עמדת היהדות , לפיה השבת מתחילה ביום שישי בערב.

title: ספר העיתים
enDesc: Sefer HaItim is a code of Jewish law by Rabbi Yehuda ben Barzillai of Barcelona. Written in the 12th century, it remained in manuscript form for hundreds of years, but its content was largely preserved through frequent quotations in works of later medieval legal decisors, an indication of the esteem in which it was held. Much of the original work was lost, and the remaining extant section, on Shabbat, is incomplete. The text was prepared for publication in the early 20th century by Rabbi Yaakov Schorr and was printed with his commentary Itim LeBinah; a number of additional paragraphs of the work have since been recovered.
enShortDesc: 12th-century code of Jewish law of which only the section on Shabbat is extant.

title: איסור והיתר לרבנו ירוחם
enDesc: Issur v’Heter l’Rabbeinu Yerucham is a 13th or 14th-century composition on dietary laws. First published in the 19th century by Rabbi Avraham Abukara, the work was mistakenly attributed to the Spanish medieval legal authority Rabbeinu Yerucham ben Meshullam. Later scholarship demonstrated that the work was actually authored by a French rabbi bearing the name “Yerucham,” a student of the Tosafist Rabbeinu Peretz . The work is based heavily on the teachings of Rabbeinu Peretz and the Sha’arei Dura, as well as on the Sefer HaTerumah, Sefer Mitzvot Gadol and Sefer Mitzvot Katan. It is quoted frequently in the Beit Yosef.
enShortDesc: Medieval composition on dietary laws published in the 19th century.
heShortDesc: חיבור מימי הביניים העוסק בהלכות כשרות. פורסם לראשונה במאה ה-19.

title: סידור רשי
enDesc: Siddur Rashi is a medieval compilation of laws about prayers. First published from manuscript in the early 20th century by Solomon Buber and Jacob Freimann, the work is attributed in its manuscripts to the celebrated 11th-century Torah scholar Rabbi Shlomo ben Yitzchak, known as Rashi.
enShortDesc: Medieval work of laws about prayers, attributed to the renowned 11th-century scholar known as Rashi.

title: שער המים הארוך
enDesc: Sha’ar HaMayim HaArokh is a short 13th-century compilation of laws about the mikvah (ritual bath) by the Rashba (Rabbi Shlomo ben Avraham ibn Aderet). It presents rulings, explanation, and analysis of topics like valid sources of water for a mikvah and conditions that disqualify a mikvah. The Rashba later wrote a condensed version, the Sha’ar HaMayim HaKatzar, in which he only presented the actual laws. These works are found in the back of some manuscripts of the Rashba’s Torat haBayit and are quoted by commentators like the Rivash, the Tashbetz and the Beit Yosef.
enShortDesc: 13th-century short compilation of laws about the mikvah (ritual bath) by the Rashba.
heShortDesc: אוסף הלכות על דיני מקוואות שנכתב על ידי הרשב"א במאה ה-13.

title: מחזור ויטרי
enDesc: Machzor Vitry is an 11th-century prayer book that incorporates legal rulings, composed by Rabbi Simcha of Vitry, a French scholar and disciple of Rashi. The word “machzor” (cycle) signifies that in addition to daily prayers, the book includes prayers for unique days on the Jewish calendar, like Shabbat, holidays, and fast days. Also incorporated are commentary on the Ten Commandments and Pirkei Avot, liturgical poems, descriptions of messianic times, and legal sections on marriage, holidays, and ritual slaughter, among other topics. The work incorporates many of Rashi’s decisions as well as decisions of other major authorities and is considered a critical source of French liturgy traditions.
enShortDesc: 11th-century prayer book that incorporates legal rulings on prayer and other topics.
heShortDesc: סידור תפילה מן המאה ה-11 המשלב פסקי הלכה הנוגעים לתפילה ולנושאים אחרים.

title: לקוטי הפרדס
enDesc: Likkutei HaPardes is a collection of legal material attributed to Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo ben Yitzchak) and is part of a body of literature known as Sifrei DeVei Rashi (Works of the School of Rashi), compiled by Rashi’s students. The first such collection to be published (1519), Likkutei HaPardes includes much of the same content as the longer Sefer HaPardes, which was not published until 1807. The collection is arranged topically and includes laws related to marriage, blessings, the Kaddish prayer, visiting the sick, holidays, and Torah readings.
enShortDesc: Early medieval collection of legal material relating to a variety of topics, attributed to Rashi and compiled by his students.

title: בעלי הנפש
enDesc: Ba’alei HaNefesh is a 12th-century work by the Ra’avad (Rabbi Avraham ben David) on the laws of niddah (a woman in her menstrual cycle or experiencing particular discharges) and sexual conduct. The work has been published in dozens of editions, and is quoted often in later legal works.
enShortDesc: 12th-century work by the Ra’avad on the laws of niddah and sexual conduct.
heDesc: ״בעלי הנפש״ הוא ספר העוסק בענייני זוגיות ונכתב במאה ה-12 על ידי אברהם בן דוד מפּוֹשְקְיֶרָה (המכונה גם: הראב״ד) בפרובאנס, צרפת. הספר מחולק לשבעה ״שערים״ כאשר ששת השערים הראשונים עוסקים בצד ההלכתי יותר של הזוגיות - הלכות נדה הקובעות מתי על בני-זוג להימנע מקיום יחסי אישות בהתאם לווסת של האישה. השער האחרון, ״שער הקדושה״, עוסק בצד הרעיוני של הזוגיות בכלל ושל יחסי אישות בפרט. לפני שבעת ה״שערים״, מביא המחבר הקדמה בה הוא מסביר כי על האדם להיות בעליה של נפשו ולמשול בה על מנת להיבדל משאר בעלי החיים. בנוסף, הוא מדגיש, בהתבססו על מקורות חז״ל, כי על האדם  ״לאהוב אשתו כגופו, ולכבדה יותר מגופו, ולרחם עליה ולשמרה כאשר ישמור אדם אחד מאבריו״ (הקדמת המחבר, פסקה ה).
heShortDesc: ״בעלי הנפש״ הוא ספר העוסק בעניינים שבינו לבינה. הספר מחולק לששה ״שערים״ הלכתיים ושער אחרון רעיוני. נכתב על ידי אברהם בן דוד מפּוֹשְקְיֶרָה (הראב״ד) במאה ה-12 בפרובאנס, צרפת.

title: העמק שאלה על שאילתות דרב אחאי גאון
enTitle: Haamek Sheilah on Sheiltot d'Rav Achai Gaon
enDesc: Extensive commentary on Sheiltot D'Rav Achai by Rabbi Naphtali Tzvi Yehuda Berlin (Netziv).
enShortDesc: 19th-century analytic commentary by the Netziv, groundbreaking in its systematic treatment of a geonic work.
heDesc: באור רחב על השאלתות של רב אחאי גאון לר' נפתלי צבי יהודה ברלין.

title: עין יוסף על ספר המצוות
enShortDesc: 20th-century commentary by Rabbi Yosef Farber, published posthumously based on classes he delivered in his yeshiva in Lithuania.

title: זוהר הרקיע
enShortDesc: 15th-century commentary on the Azharot of Solomon ibn Gabirol, summarizing methods of enumerating the 613 commandments.

title: הגהות הרדל על ספר הפרנס
enTitle: Haggahot of Radal on Sefer HaParnas
enDesc: 19th-century glosses on the beginning of a medieval collection of the Maharam of Rothenburg’s rulings and traditions by Rabbi David Luria, known by the acronym "Radal."
enShortDesc: 19th-century glosses on the beginning of a medieval collection of the Maharam of Rothenburg’s rulings and traditions by R. David Luria

title: בדק הבית על תורת הבית הארוך
enTitle: Bedek HaBayit on Torat HaBayit HaArokh
enDesc: Written by Rabbi Aharon HaLevi (Ra’ah), Bedek HaBayit on Torat HaBayit HaArokh is a criticism of Rashba’s work. Rashba answered the critique in his own book, Mishmeret HaBayit.
enShortDesc: 13th-century critical commentary of Ra’ah on Rashba’s manual on kashrut, niddah, and mikvah immersion

title: ברית עולם על ספר חסידים
enDesc: A commentary on the medieval pietistic work of R. Yehudah Hachasid, Brit Olam is one of many works by Rabbi Hayyim Joseph David Azulay.
enShortDesc: 18th-century commentary of the Chida on the foundational work of medieval German pietists.

title: הגהות חדשות על ספר מצוות קטן
enTitle: Haggahot Chadashot on Sefer Mitzvot Katan
enShortDesc: 18th-century commentary by Rabbi Yehoshua Tzeitlish of Shklov elucidating the text of the Semak and analyzing it against the backdrop of earlier sources.

title: משמרת הבית על תורת הבית הארוך
enTitle: Mishmeret HaBayit on Torat HaBayit HaAroch
enDesc: Mishmeret HaBayit is the Rashba’s response to Ra’ah’s critique of his work, Torat HaBayit HaKatzar. Ra’ah’s critique is called Bedek HaBayit.
enShortDesc: 13th-century response of the Rashba to Bedek HaBayit, the Re’ah’s critique of the Rashba’s Torat HaBayit.

title: תועפות ראם
enDesc: Commentary on Sefer Yereim by the first publisher of the complete version of the book
enShortDesc: 19th-century commentary on Sefer Yereim added by R. Abraham Abba Schiff when he published the first complete edition of the work
heDesc: ביאור מקיף לספר יראים, חובר על ידי המו"ל הראשון של הספר השלם.

heAuthors: משה אהרן בן אברהם חיים וייס
title: ברית משה
enDesc: Exhaustive commentary on Sefer Mitzvot Gadol (Semag).
enShortDesc: 20th-century exhaustive commentary on the Semag (Sefer Mitzvot Gadol) by Rabbi Moshe Aaron Weisz.
heDesc: ביאור מקיף על 'ספר מצוות גדול' (סמ"ג).

title: שאילת שלום על שאילתות דרב אחאי גאון
enTitle: Sheilat Shalom on Sheiltot d'Rav Achai Gaon
enShortDesc: 18th-century commentary by Rabbi Yeshaya Berlin analyzing the text of the Sheiltot in light of talmudic passages and earlier commentators.

title: הגהות רבנו פרץ על ספר מצוות קטן
enTitle: Haggahot Rabbeinu Peretz on Sefer Mitzvot Katan
enDesc: Glosses on "Sefer Mitzvot Katan" by the author's student, R' Peretz of Corbeil.
enShortDesc: 13th-century glosses on the Semak by the author's student, the French Tosafist Rabbeinu Peretz of Corbeil.
heDesc: הגהות על ספר "ספר מצוות קטן" על ידי תלמיד של המחבר, רבינו פרץ מקורביל.

title: נשמת אדם
enDesc: Parallel work to the Chayei Adam and usually printed together with it, discussing the halachic issues covered by the Chayei Adam in greater detail.

title: פירוש קדמון על ספר חסידים
